milestone: A Frame Style Gallery of 10 ready-made looks, a reorganized and relabeled field editor with a genuine Solid Colour option and a Transparent toggle on every colour field, a transparent-by-default baseline for a brand-new Frame, a collapsed Manage Frames list, Experience-as-Frame tucked under an (Advanced) details element, and Builder's own preview finally showing what Mat Surface/Frame Style actually do
slice: The user's own words, scoped without ambiguity: "designing a place/frame is really complicated. we need to simplify it." -> "the entire concept of place and frame. we need to simplify it." -> asked style-presets-plus-collapse-advanced vs. reorganize/relabel vs. both, the answer was "Both." A mid-implementation "wait" interruption was followed by four further, concrete requirements in one message: the editing view must show what's actually being edited (it looked stuck on background colour); every colour control needs a Transparent option; an uncustomized Place should render exactly like Transparent, since it's just a hook otherwise; and Manage Frames showing every Frame at once was confusing. Two Explore agents plus a Plan agent found the real shape of the mess: 11 raw, jargon-named fields with no "just pick a good look" path; background/frame/paper silently defaulted since the Asset Repository Transition sprint with zero authoring UI ever built; Corner Radius/Inset were two more raw controls nobody understood; there was no real "pick any colour" mat option; and -- the fidelity gap that would have undermined everything -- Frame's background/frame(ornament) choice was read by root Studio's real renderer but read NOWHERE in Builder's own preview (_paintHolder hardcoded the mat fill to a flat #F5F2EA regardless of background, and never touched corner radius/ornament from frame at all). New js/services/framePresets.js (window.FramePresets.CATALOG, 10 entries -- Classic White/Warm Ivory/Natural Linen/Dark Gallery/Floating Frame/Black Matte/Gold Ornate/Snapshot Corkboard/Polaroid Snap/Taped Sketch; the first 7's matWidth/frameThickness/borderColor/wallTone/shadow transcribed verbatim from the real, already-authored official-worlds/MuseumGallery/frames/*.json files) backs a new _renderFrameStyleGallery(project) at the top of the Frames screen -- clicking a card mints a brand-new Frame (never reuses/dedupes), applies every preset field, uniquifies the name via a new ProjectModel._uniqueFrameName, and lands the author directly on the field editor, already good-looking. The field editor is reorganized and relabeled -- Frame Name | Wall Colour, Mat Surface (gains a genuine 'color'/Solid Colour option) | Frame Style, a conditional Solid Colour swatch or Background-Image picker+Rotation, Border Color (alone -- Corner Radius's control removed outright), Shadow | Paper Texture (new, replaces Shadow|Inset), Mat Width | Wall Margin, Border Thickness, Description. _ensureFrameFieldDefaults gains matColor plus three new booleans (wallToneTransparent/borderColorTransparent/matColorTransparent), mirroring the exact Colour-Experience-content convention already shipped; a new _colorInputWithTransparent renders a swatch plus an always-visible Transparent checkbox on Wall Colour/Solid Colour/Border Color alike. A genuinely new _defaultFrameFields() (used only by a plain '+ Create Frame') sets every value EXPLICITLY to a transparent baseline (background:'transparent', frame:'none', matWidth/frameThickness/defaultMargin:0, every *Transparent flag true, shadow:'none') rather than leaving anything undefined, so a brand-new, uncustomized Frame now renders with zero visible wall/border/mat/shadow -- exactly like a Place with no Frame at all. The saved-Frames list collapses behind a <details> ("Your Frames (N)"), open by default only at 0-1 Frames. The two fidelity gaps close together in engineRuntime.js's _paintHolder: a new MAT_MATERIAL_FILL table mirrors root Studio's real ARTWORK_BACKGROUND_FILL exactly, so background's chosen value now genuinely renders distinctly in Builder's own preview; a new FRAME_ORNAMENT_PRESET table mirrors ARTWORK_FRAME_PRESET's own cornerRadius values -- the one disclosed, intentional visual-change consequence of this sprint: corner radius is now always DERIVED from Frame Style instead of read from the removed raw cornerRadius control. A new, lightweight _paintFrameOrnament adds one small distinguishing visual cue per ornament value beyond corner radius alone (wood grain-lines, a polaroid caption-line, tape corner tints, bulletin-board pins). Experience-as-Frame is wrapped in a collapsed <details> ("Reuse this Frame as an Experience (Advanced)") -- a real bug was found and fixed while building this: the details' own open computation only considered whether a Frame Experience was already attached, but clicking Add Experience triggers a full panel re-render via shared module state and silently re-collapsed around the very form the click had just opened; fixed by also checking the in-progress quick-create/reuse flags. Verified via a 57-assertion Playwright suite covering Gallery creation, the relabeled/removed controls, Solid Colour/Paper Texture persistence, the Experience-as-Frame collapse/expand (the exact assertion that caught the re-collapse bug), Builder-preview mat-fill fidelity across 6 background values, frame-style/ornament corner-radius and grain-line fidelity (with hand-verified inset arithmetic explaining exactly why a frame:'none' sharp corner correctly shows borderColor, not wallTone, when defaultMargin/inset are both 0), and backward compatibility (a legacy-shaped Frame fed through the REAL findFrame() reconciliation path now resolves to a true white mat + sharp corners, Builder's preview becoming more accurate to Studio, not diverging). A pre-existing sibling suite (feature1_frameimage_verify.js) needed one genuine, disclosed correction -- its own hardcoded 'un-imaged Frame' assertion still expected the OLD universal #F5F2EA fallback for background:'white', predating MAT_MATERIAL_FILL; corrected to expect real white, the deliberate, intended consequence of this sprint's own fix, not a regression -- now 18/18. Full regression: both goldenBuild.js suites (World Builder v1 and v2) PASS unchanged; museum_realfile_pixelhash.js (the real, on-disk Museum Gallery .vtheme rendered through root Studio's own pipeline) SHA-256-hashes byte-identical to this project's own recorded history, confirming root Studio is completely unaffected, exactly as scoped; manageframes_inline_rotation_verify2.js (16/16); place_guardrails_runtime_verify.js (10/10); scene_dropdown_repro3.js (14/14). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js, tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js, tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js, tools/world-builder-v2/css/world-builder.css, and a new tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/framePresets.js.
